Alex — great questions. Quick answers inline and a small update to the measurement plan below.

- Concurrency: yes — we’ll run two primary configurations: (A) baseline: 8 concurrent sessions, sustained 250 qps; (B) stress: 12 concurrent sessions, peak bursts to 400 qps for 60s intervals.

- KV cache simulation: our harness can simulate repeated prefixes and maintain a configurable cache hit rate. Proposed plan: run with a cold-start pass (0% cache hits), then a warmed pass (target 65% hit rate) to show delta. We’ll include measured cache-hit ratio in the results.

- Model variants: we will run three variants in this order: FP16 baseline -> 8-bit quantized -> 4-bit experimental (if available). Results will show latency and quality deltas. If you only want quantization + baseline, we can skip the 4-bit run.

MeasurementSpec updates (summary of what we changed in measurement_spec_v1.md):
- Warmup: 5 minutes or 10k tokens, whichever comes first.
- Steady windows: three 10-minute windows, non-overlapping, report p50/p90/p95/p99, error rates, and streaming chunk latencies.
- Repro artifacts: runner seed, model checksum, runner config, raw per-request logs (anonymized), and perf traces.
- Retention note for procurement: benchmarking logs include request id, timestamp, token counts, and anonymized prompt id. No PII; raw prompt text is kept only for agreed runs and can be redacted on request. Retention: artifacts kept for 30 days by default; can be shortened in writing.

Next steps:
- Monica will send a calendar invite for a 2-hour slot (your choice of 6/16 afternoon or 6/17 afternoon PST).
- Emily to send the redacted transcript sample.
- Confirm whether you want the 4-bit experimental run.

If that all works I’ll kick off runner config and share the exact command-line harness invocation so your SREs can verify.
